gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the Epson PowerLite L690U it recommended has a built-in HDBaseT receiver, so one Cat5e-or-better STP cable up to 100 m from the booth plus Epson's ELPHD02 transmitter (which ships with its own AC adapter) replaces a long HDMI run, or that turning on HDBaseT Control Communications switches off the projector's own LAN and RS-232C ports.
standout_why: I read projectorcentral.com 'Top 10 House of Worship Church Projectors November 2026'. It never mentions HDBaseT, extenders or how to power a transmitter. Its only point about long runs is 3G-SDI on two Epson EB-PU models. I also read projectorverdict.com 'Best Projector for Church 2026'. It has no HDBaseT or extender content: it describes a volunteer re-running an HDMI cable across the platform every week, offers Miracast as the fix, and says only that most projectors use M4 screw points. Neither page and neither ChatGPT answer explains how to get the booth computer's signal to a ceiling-mounted L690U, PT-VMZ62 or LU935. This is a 2 rather than a 3 because I couldn't confirm from Epson whether the L690U's HDBaseT port powers a transmitter, so I can't yet say whether a cheaper third-party transmitter powered over the cable (PoC) would work.
kit_items: projector: Epson PowerLite L690U (V11HB29020), 6,500 lm WUXGA laser. Its connector list in the manual includes 1 HDBaseT port (RJ-45) next to HDMI1, HDMI2 and HDMI Out, so no separate HDBaseT receiver is needed.

HDBaseT transmitter: Epson ELPHD02 (V12H007A14). Epson lists it as an optional accessory on the L690U product page. It has 2 HDMI inputs plus USB-A/B and ships with an AC adapter, so it doesn't depend on the projector for power.
cable: Category 5e STP or better (shielded), up to 100 m from the transmitter to the projector's HDBaseT port, per the L690U User's Guide.

ceiling mount: Epson ELPMB22 (V12H003B22) or the low-profile ELPMB30, plus the ELPWR01 safety wire set. The L690U-series User's Guide names these three. Note that the ELPMB22 product page's 'Works With' list does not include the L690U.

findings.label: HDBaseT port
findings.value: 1 × HDBaseT (RJ-45), alongside HDMI1, HDMI2, HDMI Out, LAN (RJ-45), RS-232C (mini D-sub 9-pin), Audio Out (stereo mini, 2 Vrms), 2 × USB-A
findings.source_title: Epson User's Guide (EB-L890E/L690U series): Connector Specifications
findings.note: The page is filed under EBL890E, but the same guide's spec page lists EB-L690U as one of the models it covers. The Epson product page also says 'HDBaseT and HDMI two in and one out'. HDMI audio is PCM only.

findings.label: HDBaseT cable requirement
findings.value: Category 5e STP or better; network cable up to 100 m
findings.source_title: Epson User's Guide: Connecting to an HDBaseT Transmitter
findings.note: Epson says to turn off both devices before plugging or unplugging the cable, and that 'operation is not guaranteed for all input/output devices and environments.'

findings.label: HDBaseT exclusion: Control Communications disables projector LAN/RS-232C
findings.value: Operation > HDBaseT > Control Communications = On enables the transmitter's Ethernet and serial ports and disables the projector's own LAN and RS-232C ports
findings.source_title: Epson User's Guide: Connecting to an HDBaseT Transmitter
findings.note: With an Extron XTP transmitter or switcher, set Extron XTP = On. To control the projector over HDBaseT while it is in standby, set Standby Mode = Normal.

findings.label: Transmitter inputs and power
findings.value: 2 × HDMI + USB-A/B inputs; box contains HDBaseT transmitter, AC power adapter, power adapter holder, USB cable, user's guide; $346.00
findings.source_title: HDBaseT Transmitter/Control Pad ELPHD02 | Epson US
findings.note: The 'Works With' tab lists the PowerLite L690U. The page gives no maximum cable length, so the 100 m figure comes from the projector's User's Guide.

findings.label: Epson store price and stock
findings.source_title: PowerLite L690U 6,500-Lumen WUXGA 3LCD Laser Projector | Epson US
findings.note: This matches the $3,515.00 ChatGPT showed. The optional accessories on the page include ELPHD02 and the Universal Projector Mount ELPMBPJG.

findings.label: Power draw and input
findings.value: 100–240 V AC, 4.4–2.0 A; 415 W Normal, 305 W Quiet, 287 W Extended (100–120 V area)
findings.note: Matters when putting the ceiling outlet on a shared circuit.

findings.label: Mounts named by the manual
findings.value: Ceiling mount ELPMB22; low-profile ceiling mount ELPMB30; safety wire set ELPWR01
findings.note: The safety wire attaches with one M4 × 10 mm screw to the wire clamp fixing point (https://files.support.epson.com/docid/cpd6/cpd65465/EN/Setup/Tasks/attaching_mount_plate_mb22.html). Epson warns not to attach it to the security cable point.

findings.label: Price and listed compatibility
findings.value: $230.00; 'Works With' lists L630SU, L630U, L730U, L520U, L520W, L530U, 815E, 810E (no L690U)
findings.note: The store page and the L690U manual disagree. The manual (above) names ELPMB22 for this series, so confirm with Epson before putting it in the cart.
